CRUEL makes me wish for a neutral review button for Steam because I enjoy some parts of it but I'm really not a fan of others. It's dingy, violent, neon, and polygonal in the most attractive ways. It nails a retraux occult atmosphere. The movement feels good and the guns feel better. I always inevitably found myself bobbing my head to whatever synth piece played in the background while I geared up for the incoming stage. Evidently, it is another addition to the genre subset of Post Void likes. It's clear that James Dornan is a fan of the game which is valid, it's an awesome game. However, as a result of this I don't feel uncomfortable comparing it to Post Void. I don't want to believe that the design choices were made simply to be in service to the game's title. CRUEL facilitates a frantic pace by forcing you through levels, else you die. If you can't one-tap enemies, you need to keep moving to the next room because defensive play is practically impossible. There's also health restoring sodas peppered through the rooms. It's a less graceful approach compared to Post Void's health timer and comes across as more clumsy in practice. Additionally, sodas can be given to the dog between levels for a selection of upgrades ranging from practical to very niche. Kicking enemies out of windows is hard to do a handful of times, let alone consistently enough for a frequent armor boost. In my experience, the upgrades don't even seem to work. As a result, I almost always chose to conserve my sodas or use the chance to heal up. Erik's Trick or Treat gamble is an interesting idea in theory, but I don't feel that one soda is worth the chance of ending the run entirely. Maybe it's designed more like a punch card of sorts where you get a free soda for every fifteen enemies killed? Something to reward consistent headshots and thoroughly clearing rooms that aligns with the mechanics already put into place. I firmly believe that this game could be a home run if sodas were just as valuable as upgrades and every system in the gameplay loop rewarded player skill.

i wan't to like this game, but i can't. that's not to say that there's anything wrong with the game aside from having too many mechanics to keep up with (two types of melees and the ability to throw melee weapons) while you're going through this fast paced shooter. I can never find a happy medium for my mouse sensitivity either as it's either too fast or too smooth with only a slider instead of a precise number input to adjust this setting and no mouth smoothing. It's probably not a game for me even though I've played other games like "I AM YOUR BEAST" and "Anger Foot" which is a shame cuz the music is great and i kinda like the look of it and i don't mind the fast past shooter action of the game, you just run out of bullets way too quickly if you solely rely on your guns, and i'm still trying to find a comfortable set up for my "kick" and "melee" and "through melee" binds so that i can easily commit them to memory. (cuz for some reason throwing melee weapons is more deadly than shooting someone...) Maybe someone else i know might like this game, but for me I can't recommend it. I'm going to give it a few more tried before I return it to see if I can get a better hang of it and find a more suitable layout for my controls.

（评测于游戏0.8.8版本后更新，基于0.6.6评测修改） 打起来很畅快的游戏，在废弃公寓楼中与身后的大火赛跑，路途上干掉各种奇形怪状的敌人 最终向某“人”复仇、 每一次的开始要输入一个人的姓名，作为杀戮到最后的复仇对象，搞笑的是我输入GOD其实也没什么彩蛋 游戏似乎只是把他判定成普通人名的样子 游戏中0.6.6版只有三种枪械，近战若干 手枪点头，散弹护身，冲锋枪泼水，定位明确，现在0.8.8还加多了一把杠杆步枪，发射的子弹可以穿透敌人 对于我这种喜欢打枪的玩家来说非常棒 游戏的近战武器就没那么出彩了 近战武器可以劈砍敌人，甚至可以格挡敌人的子弹，但是风险很大，因为近战武器没有办法一击杀死人形敌人（除非爆头），而格挡敌人子弹还不如轻松AD躲避用枪反击 目前只有10层可以攻克，每攻克完1层可以给小狗喝饮料roll一个加强 加强的数量其实没有那么多，而且还是有一些没什么卵用的加强，0.8.8没什么卵用的加强还更多了 类似踢击敌人可以让被飞出去敌人击中的敌人着火，近战格挡敌人子弹可以恢复弹药量等等 加上新版本地图设计的更加弯弯绕 感觉是作者想让玩家多用用近战武器和踢击，但是实际体验下来还是专攻枪械比较好 个人推荐类似提升换弹速度，增加备弹量，增加弹药拾取量，还有提升血上限这几样 到6层之后基本都是枪械大杀特杀的时候了，那时候还执着于近战很容易出事情... 敌人的爆头判定也很严格，需要更仔细的瞄准才行，如果能把爆头判定再稍微扩大一点感觉会更好 在游玩的过程中，你就会不知不觉成为一个无情的爆头机器 但是游戏玩到7层及以后就会明显感觉力不从心 7层的敌人种类已经变得很多了，而且场景中也会出现很多陷阱 最神的一个地形就是一个丁字口，前面有门会刷怪，左边长走廊有怪，右边拐角也有怪 你走到中间一群傻逼就会冲出来强暴你 这就是整个游戏变得混乱的地方，你的能耐再牛逼能挡得住四面八方的自杀式袭击吗？ 到后面运气成分就占得更多了，遇到这种极端情况很容易就会掉很多血量 更别提还有这种真正意义上火烧屁股的游戏机制了 0.8.8更新改进了一些老版本的初见杀怪物 例如老版本的重甲条子，现在变成了精神病人可以被爆头了，但他仍然会用格挡你的近战攻击（有几率格挡） 炸药桶自爆哥布林变成了自爆骷髅，而且他被击杀之后会被打飞，更不容易伤害到玩家，自爆还有明显前摇，非常好的改进 游戏还有若干模式，例如无尽模式，完美模式（无法用饮料回血），禁枪模式等 这些模式里我只体验了下无尽模式，初始让你选3个perk，然后就闯关，有个成就是打到无尽模式20关，但是我打到13关就顶不住了，并不是因为我挂掉了，而是因为太累了 从第10关开始就是最高难度，敌人非常多，每一层都非常长不是说不能打只是太熬人 所以作罢，如果你以为无尽模式也是每层能roll perk叠到最后满状态泥头车力大砖飞可以放弃了，我一开始也以为是能叠perk乱创，这游戏还是老实玩闯关模式最实在 总体玩起来比较流畅，如果你喜欢把敌人脑袋爆的开花可以尝试一下 游戏比较考验fps基本功和反应力，就算这把roll到的perk全是下水道 只要枪刚反应快，照样能打通关，perk主要还是起锦上添花的作用 但是如果不习惯玩FPS就不推荐玩了，因为各种高速转视角很有可能让你头晕脑胀 而且进游戏记得把一些画面效果关上，例如画面抖动闪屏之类的，能显著提升游玩体验，但是居然不能改FOV吗？ 只能说幸好默认FOV距离较广，至少有个100~105吧，不然真的样衰了 突击到10层之后，终于见到了复仇对象，但他居然是...？

It seems I am in the minority when it comes to having mixed feelings about the game. I do believe the game has a lot to love, but it's what it lacks that is the problem. The amount of praise and hype it receives has made me question my own stance about it. Maybe I am just being overly critical or too particular in what I look for, cause it's pretty clear I have a hot take. Firstly, I really wish there was a stronger sense of long-term progression. Most roguelikes reward you over time by letting you unlock new abilities, weapons, enemies, items, or even changes to the levels themselves. There is usually some kind of growth, even during a single deep run. But this game does not offer any of that. When you die, you are forced to restart from the very beginning with nothing to show for it. Unless you manage to reach the end, which is extremely difficult in the early game, you walk away with absolutely nothing. And the end is the end. The only thing you unlock is a new game mode with no weapons and the other game-mode is probably similar to that like some mechanic taken away instead of new ones being added. I know that might seem fine on paper, since it raises the stakes and makes each run feel more intense. It is definitely more focused and nerve-racking when you know that one death means starting over. That being said, the best roguelikes usually give you some incentive to keep going after failure. This game gives you nothing. I understand that it is supposed to be punishing, but this feels less like a deliberate design choice and more like a lack of progression systems. It just feels empty. The level layouts are also very repetitive and lack the intricacy or variety that would make them stand out. You can trade sodas for abilities, but sodas are your main healing source. Giving them up means losing an important health option that you might need later. The abilities you get in return are usually so weak that they barely impact your run. Moreover, there are only like 5 different abilities and none of them are even remotely fun to use imo. There are better roguelike FPS games out there that are more fun and exciting to play. Roboquest, for example, is a stronger game overall, though it is also more complex. This game is intentionally simpler and is clearly inspired by 90s shooters. Post Void has that same old-school feel but also adds its own unique twist. Mullet Mad Jack offers more refined gameplay and deeper mechanics, but it is also more layered. Nightmare reaper is another good one that comes to mind. This game, by comparison, embraces a stripped-down design. The creepy art style and 90s theme work well together, and the enemy designs match the tone perfectly. The combat and movement are challenging, but they feel responsive and satisfying. The visuals are great. There are some cool features too, like blocking bullets with melee weapons, throwing them to conserve ammo, or using them when you are out of bullets. The enemy encounters are fun, even though the enemy variety is limited. This game embraces the idea that less is more. But it also comes at the expense of mechanics that could have heavily improved on the core aspects of the game and give it more replay value. I am mixed on the game, but I think it is worth checking out if it even slightly appeals to you. Just keep in mind that there are stronger games in this genre. What makes this one stand out is its visual identity and style, which give it a fresh and memorable feel. It just does not feel fully complete. I recommend picking it up on sale, but not for the full price of $10. I am hoping the dev will add more content. More weapons, power cards, levels, etc. anything that will increase longevity and replay ability. I really doubt they will though cause that takes a lot of effort and I think it would have already happened by now. I had to uninstall this game after beating it cause I really don't feel like getting trapped in its horrendous death cycle again.

I bought this game because I loved the fast pace, flashy visuals and great soundtrack. It looked like a very honest FPS adaptation of Hotline Miami. However the difficulty is punishing, and starting from the beginning every time for a game you know you probably won't be able to beat is frustrating. Perhaps in time an update will allow for some form of player progression so I have a chance in hell I'll consider picking it up again. It's an amusing way to spend a few minutes but unless you enjoy slamming your head against a wall for hours on end I can't recommend it.

I like this game BUT it really should be listed as an 'early access' title currently, not a full release. As of June 2026 it is quite lean in just about all aspects outside of its core gameplay loop. CRUEL has a fantastic tone, upheld by grimy horror inspired visuals and music that evokes much of the same feeling. Its core run and gun gameplay is visceral, feeling generally great for the most part. However, the games' roguelike elements are severely under-baked currently, primarily in it's card modifiers, enemy pool & environmental design, leading to each run being fairly 'samey'; whilst small things like some wonky hit boxes and enemy readability also hamper the experience. Ultimately I recommend it because of its cheap price point, however, i'd ALSO recommend waiting a while and letting this game cook in the oven a bit more.

When you get ahold of CRUEL's gameplay loop, you will enter a FLOW STATE. Pop a headshot, kick cultist out the window, roll over and grab his melee weapon, slice up three enemies who are charging straight at you, toss the melee weapon down the hall at another poor cultist, vandalize a vending machine and chug its contents, yadayadayada. CRUEL's gameplay loop is a total blast and is supported by powerful and satisfying weapons, a varied and fleshed out enemy roster, and super tight controls. CRUEL's levels are procedurally generated which does mean they don't have a handcrafted feel, but the level layouts are never exactly the same, and it keeps you on your toes. CRUEL'S SOUNDTRACK is high energy, fast tempo electronic music of various types and it does a stellar job of motivating the player to keep moving forward at a breakneck pace. One of my favorite elements of the game easily. This game doesn't have the most content, but there are various side modes and I've been having so much fun trying to beat them for all the achievements. I also love CRUEL'S GRUNGY and SILLY ATMOSPHERE. CRUEL rules and deserves to be talked about more

CRUEL is a relentless first-person shooter that captures the intensity of classic boomer shooters while introducing an innovative mechanic that constantly changes the battlefield beneath the player's feet. Developed and published by James Dornan, the game places speed, precision, and adaptability above everything else. Rather than relying on an elaborate story, it focuses on delivering a pure gameplay experience where every level becomes a desperate fight for survival. Its straightforward premise allows the mechanics to take center stage, creating a satisfying experience for players who appreciate skill-driven action and nonstop combat. The most distinctive aspect of CRUEL is its ever-changing environment. Instead of navigating static maps, players find themselves in levels that transform as they progress, with walls shifting, pathways opening, and familiar routes disappearing. This dynamic system forces players to remain alert throughout every encounter since memorizing a layout offers little advantage. The evolving architecture not only keeps exploration engaging but also affects combat by creating unexpected opportunities and fresh dangers. Every run feels different, giving the game considerable replay value while maintaining a constant sense of uncertainty. Combat is designed around movement and aggression. Standing still is rarely an option, as enemies relentlessly pursue the player through increasingly dangerous arenas. A varied arsenal provides tools for different situations, encouraging players to switch weapons depending on enemy behavior and battlefield conditions. The controls feel responsive, allowing fluid movement while firing, dodging, and repositioning during intense firefights. Success depends on maintaining momentum, managing resources effectively, and reacting quickly to rapidly changing situations instead of relying solely on overwhelming firepower. Enemy variety contributes significantly to the challenge. Each opponent introduces different attack styles and movement patterns, preventing encounters from becoming repetitive. As levels continue to shift during battle, players must constantly reconsider their positioning and priorities, making every confrontation feel unpredictable. The combination of aggressive enemies and dynamic environments creates an exhilarating gameplay loop that rewards careful observation, quick reflexes, and strategic decision-making without sacrificing the fast pace expected from the genre. The visual presentation embraces retro-inspired aesthetics while incorporating modern graphical enhancements. Its gritty environments, atmospheric lighting, and detailed effects successfully recreate the spirit of classic shooters without feeling outdated. Blood-soaked corridors, industrial structures, and unsettling architecture establish a harsh atmosphere that perfectly complements the game's brutal tone. The visual clarity also serves gameplay well, ensuring enemies and environmental changes remain easy to recognize even during the most chaotic battles. Audio design plays an equally important role in reinforcing the experience. Powerful weapon effects make every shot feel impactful, while enemy sounds provide valuable cues during combat. The energetic soundtrack sustains the game's relentless pace, encouraging players to stay aggressive and maintain momentum. Together, the music and sound effects enhance immersion and make victories feel even more rewarding after surviving difficult encounters. Replayability is one of CRUEL's strongest qualities. Because the environments continuously evolve and encounters rarely unfold the same way twice, each playthrough presents new tactical possibilities. Players can experiment with different weapon combinations, movement strategies, and approaches to overcoming increasingly difficult situations. This emphasis on replayability ensures that mastering the game remains an engaging process rather than a repetitive grind. CRUEL successfully modernizes the old-school first-person shooter formula without abandoning the core principles that made the genre popular. Its transforming levels, satisfying gunplay, relentless pacing, and strong audiovisual presentation combine to create a memorable action experience that rewards both skill and persistence. While the minimal narrative and demanding difficulty may not appeal to everyone, fans of fast-paced shooters will find a challenging and highly replayable adventure that stands out through its inventive environmental mechanics. It is an exhilarating blend of classic design philosophy and fresh gameplay innovation. Rating: 9/10

I like the game but... I think it has a lot of issues. First of all, the lack of a tutorial made it extremely confusing for me the first time I played. I also take issue with the fact that multibinding is not possible. I'd like to bind more than 1 key for melee or for weapon throwing but the game doesn't allow this. Additionally, I understand the approach of no handholding, but there's a difference between no handholding and throwing the player into a pit of venomous snakes. I'm really struggling with getting past floor 3. That's because no mechanics were explained to me at all. A game as challenging as Cruelty Squad (that famously touts "no hand holding" either) even has a tutorial. I'd like for you to be able to interact to open doors rather than having to kick them. E for throwing a weapon makes no sense. The default bindings are all over the place. Binding slide to C forces the player to either move their finger off the D key to slide, or move their finger off jump to slide. Either way is indesirable. There's a lot of potential here and I'd much prefer it to be in early access so we know that there's more features coming and updates to be made. Some things I do like is that there's multiple moves bound to one button that are contextual, for example how parrying enemy melee attacks and bullets (if you have the upgrade) is bound to the melee button. I love how meaty headshots feel and I see a lot of potential for combos in this game. There NEEDS to be an FOV slider. PLEASE. And/or a crosshair customiser. Why can't I change my resolution in the video settings? They're awfully lacking and need to be updated. There's a lot of things about this game that just feel... unfinished, despite the game not saying it's early access. I'm surprised these issues got past quality assurance. Good game so far but it needs a lot of work.

[h2]Cruel: "disposed to inflict pain or suffering : devoid of humane feelings"[/h2] How far are you willing to go to kill? 10 floors in a derelict soviet style apartment building stand between you and the answer. Every cultist, crackhead tenant, dark entity, fueled my insatiable bloodlust climaxing with a choice so Cruel, I wasn't sure of who I was anymore. Weapon variety is solid. You've got your standard fare - revolver, smg, shotgun, chainsaw, axe, among others that I'll leave you to discover. Perks after each floor in exchange for soda (health) created an interesting balance between survivability and build crafting. Would you rather enemies drop more bullets or sacrifice your last soda without knowing where the next vending machine is? Fast paced is not an exaggeration here, the fire spreading throughout the building is unrelenting and forces you to be decisive and commit to your movements and choices. Several new rituals (game modes) have been added since release including the fan favorite "endless" which adds replayability. There is little in the way of telling a story, but the incentive of completing a murder ritual was plenty of fun to me. You're not getting many options/settings here. Cruel is a tight, fun, and complete experience that I'd happily recommend to fans of fast paced intense fps combat with horror elements. I'm looking forward to whatever James Dornan decides to cook up next.

I loved this game, came at just the right time for me. Cruel is really straight-forward and simple, but it's a blast to play. It's one of those games you could probably have installed all the time to just return to whenever you had an itch. Getting started or resuming play is really quick, and it has a nice gameplay loop where things just flow perfectly. Most of it comes down to running down halls and shooting everything that moves, with a satisfying blend of some melee options. The weapons are limited so there isn't too much to learn; and it just takes practice to get good at headshots, knowing when to melee, when to throw, and how to move. When I first started it, I loved the style and graphics; and I loved the OST a ton. Even the kind of edgy writing is amusing to me, because it's not like the concept is really high class. Kind of reminds me of Postal. When you've finished the "main" roguelike part of the game, there's quite a lot of replayability because the gameplay is so good. Even more, you can try endless mode, no healing, or melee only. I would have liked to have a customization option so I could do like endless with progressive perks, or perfection with perks. Overall, I just wish there was MORE altogether. More enemies, more perks, more options. I definitely felt like I got what I paid for, but I wish it was a larger game rather than only an arcade-style. Still, I think it gets work on it occasionally, and it would take a long time to get all the achievements, so this one is definitely worth it.
